## What The Business Is

GE Vernova is a global energy-equipment and services company, not a regulated electric utility: it sells power-generation, grid, electrification, software, and wind technologies to utilities, developers, industrials, governments, and data-center-linked customers. The company describes itself as a “purpose-built global energy company” organized around **Power, Electrification, and Wind**, with roughly 85,000 employees across about 100 countries. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/news/taxonomy/term/9211))

## What It Does

The **Power** segment includes gas, nuclear, and hydro equipment and services; in Q1 2026, Power revenue was $5.0B, with Gas Power the largest contributor. **Electrification** sells grid infrastructure such as transformers, switchgear, HVDC, substations, power conversion/storage, and grid software; Q1 Electrification backlog reached $42.4B. **Wind** sells and services onshore/offshore turbines, but remains the weakest segment financially. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_10-q_04222026.pdf))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Q1 2026 was a strong demand/cash quarter: orders were **$18.3B**, up **71% organically**, backlog rose **$13.0B sequentially** to about **$163B**, free cash flow was **$4.8B**, and management raised 2026 guidance to revenue of **$44.5B–$45.5B**, adjusted EBITDA margin of **12%–14%**, and free cash flow of **$6.5B–$7.5B**. The transcript also emphasized that total backlog is now expected to reach **$200B in 2027**, a year earlier than prior expectations. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_pressrelease_04222026.pdf))

Power demand remained a central positive. GE Vernova said Gas Power backlog plus slot-reservation agreements rose to **100 GW** in Q1, and in June it booked a Q2 order to supply **two 9HA.02 gas turbines and two H78 generators** for EVN’s Quang Trach II LNG plant in Vietnam, a project expected to produce more than **1.6 GW** by 2030. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_pressrelease_04222026.pdf))

Electrification momentum also strengthened. Management said Q1 Electrification equipment orders for data centers were **$2.4B**, more than full-year 2025, while the Prolec GE transformer acquisition added scale and backlog. GE Vernova also launched **GridOS for Transmission** in June, positioning grid software as a response to surging load, renewable integration, and faster grid operations. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_pressrelease_04222026.pdf))

Nuclear/SMR optionality remains a visible growth theme: the U.S. and Japan announced up to **$40B** for GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 SMRs in Tennessee and Alabama, with a stated **3 GW** capacity target. GE Vernova Hitachi also expanded a European BWRX-300 supplier collaboration with Velan in June. ([commerce.gov](https://www.commerce.gov/news/fact-sheets/2026/03/fact-sheet-new-energy-projects-us-japan-trade-deal))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Wind remains the main operational drag. In Q1 2026, Wind revenue fell **25% organically**, segment EBITDA loss widened to **$(382)M**, and management attributed the decline to lower onshore equipment deliveries, tariff impacts, and higher offshore contract losses; 2026 Wind guidance still called for about **$400M** of segment EBITDA losses. ([gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_presentation_04222026.pdf))

Offshore Wind legal/project risk stayed in focus. In April, Vineyard Wind sued GE Renewables/GE Vernova-related entities after a contract-payment dispute tied to the 2024 blade failure; AP reported GE

## Bull Case
- Record demand: Q1 orders of $18.3B (+71% organic), backlog ~$163B and tracking toward $200B in 2027 — a year early. Gas Power backlog plus slot reservations at 100 GW gives multi-year revenue visibility.
- Electrification is inflecting: $2.4B of data-center equipment orders in Q1 alone (more than all of 2025), $42.4B segment backlog, Prolec GE transformer scale, and the GridOS software launch add margin-rich growth.
- Raised 2026 guidance: revenue $44.5–45.5B, adjusted EBITDA margin 12–14%, FCF $6.5–7.5B; Q1 FCF was already $4.8B.
- Nuclear/SMR optionality (up to $40B U.S.–Japan BWRX-300 program, 3 GW target) is essentially free upside at current earnings.
- If margins expand toward the high end of guidance and Wind losses shrink, the market can sustain a premium growth multiple (45–55x forward), pushing market cap toward $320–350B.

## Bear Case
- TTM net income of $9.4B (23.8% net margin) looks inflated versus guided adjusted EBITDA of only ~$5.4–6.3B, implying large one-time gains. Normalized forward earnings are materially lower, and the stock is effectively trading well above 30x clean earnings.
- Wind remains a structural drag: revenue -25% organically, Q1 EBITDA loss of $(382)M, ~$400M full-year losses guided, plus Vineyard Wind litigation and offshore contract-loss risk.
- Cyclical order books can decelerate; data-center capex is a crowded, sentiment-driven trade. Any order slowdown compresses the premium multiple quickly (mc history 3y std is 55% of mean — extreme volatility).
- Tariffs, supply-chain cost inflation in turbines/transformers, and execution risk on a backlog doubling in three years could pressure margins.
- At 40x a normalized $5B of net income, market cap would be ~$200B, ~30% below current levels.

## Logic
- Forward revenue: ~$45B (guidance midpoint), growing into 2027 on backlog conversion.
- Forward net income: TTM NI of $9,375M appears boosted by non-recurring items (it exceeds guided adjusted EBITDA). I normalize toward a ~13–14% net margin on ~$46B of forward revenue as margins expand and Wind losses moderate → **forward NI ≈ $6,200M**. Forward FCF anchored to guidance ≈ $7,000M.
- Applied multiple: GEV commands a premium growth multiple given backlog visibility, electrification/data-center exposure, and SMR optionality, but volatility and Wind risk cap it. I apply **~48x forward earnings** (vs. ~31x optically on inflated TTM NI, and consistent with market pricing of secular power-demand winners).
- Forward market cap: 6,200 × 48 ≈ **$297,600M**, modest upside (~3%) from the current $289.4B — strong fundamentals largely priced in.

## Bull Case
GE Vernova's demand backdrop is exceptional: Q1 2026 orders up 71% organically, backlog ~$163B heading to $200B by 2027, and FCF guidance of $6.5B–$7.5B. Power (gas turbine slot reservations at 100 GW) and Electrification (data-center transformer/grid demand) are structurally accelerating, driven by AI load growth. TTM net income already reached $9,375M vs. $1,936M a year prior—an inflection in profitability as margins scale. Forward net income could grow toward ~$11.5B on revenue guidance of $44.5B–$45.5B and margin expansion. A premium growth multiple (~30x) reflecting secular energy tailwinds pushes market cap above $340B.

## Bear Case
Wind remains a persistent drag (Q1 EBITDA loss of $(382)M, ~$400M FY loss guided), and offshore litigation (Vineyard Wind) adds tail risk. TTM net income of $9,375M likely includes non-recurring items; the ni/mc ratio jump to 3.24% (vs. 1.5–1.7% historical average) suggests current earnings may be elevated or the market is pricing in normalization. Tariff impacts and execution risk on long-cycle equipment could compress margins. A more sober forward net income of ~$9B with a de-rated multiple (~22x) would put market cap near ~$200B, below current levels.

- **Forward net income:** Revenue guidance midpoint ~$45B with 13% adjusted EBITDA margin implies ~$5.85B EBITDA at segment level, but reported net income benefits from services mix, backlog conversion, and reduced Wind losses. - **Applied multiple:** Current market cap ($289.4B) implies ~30.9x TTM net income. Given strong secular growth but rich valuation and normalization risk, I apply a slightly compressed ~29x to forward net income.
- **Forward market cap:** $10,000M × 29 = ~$290,000M, roughly in line with current cap—implying the market has largely priced in near-term growth, with upside contingent on backlog execution.

GE Vernova's demand backdrop is exceptional: Q1 2026 orders up 71% organically, backlog ~$163B heading to $200B by 2027, and FCF guidance of $6.5B–$7.5B. Power (gas turbine slot reservations at 100 GW) and Electrification (data-center transformer/grid demand) are structurally accelerating, driven by AI load growth. TTM net income already reached $9,375M vs. $1,936M a year prior—an inflection in profitability as margins scale. Forward net income could grow toward ~$11.5B on revenue guidance of $44.5B–$45.5B and margin expansion. A premium growth multiple (~30x) reflecting secular energy tailwinds pushes market cap above $340B.

## Bear Case
Wind remains a persistent drag (Q1 EBITDA loss of $(382)M, ~$400M FY loss guided), and offshore litigation (Vineyard Wind) adds tail risk. TTM net income of $9,375M likely includes non-recurring items; the ni/mc ratio jump to 3.24% (vs. 1.5–1.7% historical average) suggests current earnings may be elevated or the market is pricing in normalization. Tariff impacts and execution risk on long-cycle equipment could compress margins. A more sober forward net income of ~$9B with a de-rated multiple (~22x) would put market cap near ~$200B, below current levels.

## Logic
- **TTM net income:** $9,375M, up sharply from $1,936M, signaling a genuine earnings inflection but possibly containing tax/one-time benefits.
- **Forward net income:** Revenue guidance midpoint ~$45B with 13% adjusted EBITDA margin implies ~$5.85B EBITDA at segment level, but reported net income benefits from services mix, backlog conversion, and reduced Wind losses. I normalize forward net income modestly above TTM to ~$10,000M, reflecting continued growth tempered by Wind losses and non-recurring TTM items.
- **Applied multiple:** Current market cap ($289.4B) implies ~30.9x TTM net income. Given strong secular growth but rich valuation and normalization risk, I apply a slightly compressed ~29x to forward net income.
- **Forward market cap:** $10,000M × 29 = ~$290,000M, roughly in line with current cap—implying the market has largely priced in near-term growth, with upside contingent on backlog execution.
- **Forward FCF:** guidance midpoint ~$7,000M, consistent with strong cash conversion.
